events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This is a driver-cancelled trip recorded as a rider no-show, so the fee can only stand through NS-1, which the trace checks element by element [F4][NS-0]. The location elements pass: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 while 41 m from the pickup, and his closest approach was 3 m at 21:29:20, well inside the 200 m radius the trace applies [F6][F1][NS-1]. The waiting element fails: NS-1(iii) requires more than 3 minutes of continuous presence at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, and the trace measures only 105 s inside the radius after the tap, against a 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1]. The independent timeline figures agree — arrival recorded 21:28:35, cancellation at 21:31:30 two minutes 55 s later, cumulative time within 200 m 2 min 55 s [F5][F2][F4][NS-1]. Pre-tap time near the pickup is expressly not counted, so the 21:28:35–21:29:45 period cannot be added [F2][F6][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement that he waited at least 5 minutes is a statement, and the GPS and timeline records contradict it; system records govern the conflict [F12][F2][F6][NS-1]. His chat establishes presence and findability — an arrival ping with a vehicle description at 21:29, then "Cancelling, waited too long" at 21:31 — not that the required wait elapsed; the complete two-message log gives the rider no NS-1(iii) window to arrive [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

With NS-1(iii) unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be returned in full [F7][F4][NS-2]. The refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, and the fee figure comes straight from the fare record, so no rate arithmetic is needed [F7][NS-7].

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver did not wait more than 3 continuous minutes at the pickup point after tapping "I'm Here": he tapped at 21:29:45 (F6) and cancelled at 21:31:30, so only 1 min 45 s elapsed within 200 m after the tap (F6), which fails NS-1(iii).

Counting from platform-recorded arrival at 21:28:35, the driver cancelled 2 min 55 s later (F5), still below the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii), and the cumulative time inside 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 55 s (F2).

The driver's "I'm Here" tap was 41 m from the pickup point (F6), which is within the 200 m arrival radius, so the tap itself was valid; but the waiting requirement was never met (F6), so under NS-2 no cancellation fee can stand.

The driver's written claim that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12, a post-trip statement) is contradicted by the system records: GPS shows only 2 min 55 s within 200 m (F2) and 1 min 45 s after the tap (F6), and the system records win.

The driver's own chat message at 21:31 says he was cancelling having "waited too long" (F10, F9 at 21:29), consistent with a premature cancellation minutes after arrival rather than a genuine no-show under NS-1(iii).
The cancellation fee of $6.61 on record (F7, F4) must therefore be refunded in full to the rider, since none of the NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) conditions was satisfied.
No traffic justification could salvage the cancellation's fee: there were no speed band records and no incidents on the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair (F13, F14, F15).

weaknesses: The driver did validly tap "I'm Here" at 41 m from the pickup (F6), so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied — the case turns entirely on the 3-minute wait in NS-1(iii), a margin of only a few seconds (1 min 45 s after tap per F6, 2 min 55 s from first arrival per F2/F5).
The driver has a long, busy record (976 days, 1216 trips, 0 disputes upheld, F17), which he may use to argue credibility, though system records (F2, F5, F6) trump his statement (F12).

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: closest approach to the pickup was 3 m at 21:29:20 (F1), he was stationary 21:29:25–21:31:30 only 39 m from the pickup (F3), and he tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 while 41 m from the pickup point (F6), so NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii)'s location requirement are met.

The rider was charged nothing beyond the standard $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F7), a fee that NS-0/NS-1 contemplate precisely for a driver-cancelled no-show, and no improper charge (surge multiplier 1.0×, F8) was applied.

The driver's own written statement says he waited at least 5 minutes and cancelled as a no-show (F12), and he messaged the rider "I'm here, white BYD e6" at 21:29 (F9) before messaging "Cancelling, waited too long" (F10), showing he was present and making himself findable at the pickup.
The chat record is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F11) — so the failure of these proceedings to show a rider reply is not an artefact of a missing or truncated chat log.

No external event excuses anything here: no speed-band records (F13), no traffic incidents (F14) and fair weather (F15) mean the trip conditions were ordinary, so the only question is the waiting-time arithmetic on the record.
The driver has 1216 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld no-show disputes (F17), so nothing in the profile supports treating this cancellation as button abuse rather than a genuine no-show attempt.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) is not satisfied on the system record: after the "I'm Here" tap at 21:29:45 the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s (F6), and his cumulative time within 200 m before cancelling was 2 min 55 s (F2) — both short of the > 3 min (≥ 3:01) continuous wait the clause requires. The rider will cite F2, F5 and F6 for exactly this.
The rider's complaint (cancelled "barely two minutes after arriving") matches the system record: arrival recorded 21:28:35 and cancellation 2 min 55 s later (F5), i.e. under three minutes.

The driver's statement that he waited "at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by the GPS/timeline (F2, F3, F6), and by the policy's rule that system records beat statements; the statement therefore cannot cure the shortfall.

Because the wait is under the NS-1 threshold, NS-1 cannot save the fee, and NS-2's consequence (refund of $6.61, and a possible account flag only if m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200 — which it is not, F6) is the outcome the record points to. This brief therefore asks only that the refund be the fee alone, with no account flag, rather than defending the charge.
Pre-tap time near the pickup is expressly not counted by NS-1(iii); the 21:28:35–21:29:45 period (F2, F6) therefore cannot be added to the post-tap wait.

points.response: Conceded: NS-1(i) and (ii) are met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 41 m from the pickup (F6) and was stationary 39 m away during the wait (F3), so the arrival/location half of NS-1 is satisfied; this does not decide the case, which turns on NS-1(iii).

Not contested as to amount — the only charge is the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) with no surge (F8) — but NS-0/NS-1 only make that fee chargeable if the no-show conditions hold, and NS-2 reverses it in full when they do not.

The 5-minute assertion exists only in the driver's post-trip statement (F12), which is contradicted by the system records: 1 min 45 s inside 200 m after the tap (F6) and 2 min 55 s cumulative before cancellation (F2), and under NS-1 system records beat statements; being findable is not the same as having waited the required time.

A complete, timestamped two-message chat log (F11) cuts against the driver, not for him: the only rider-side channel was the driver's 21:29 ping (F9) and he cancelled two minutes later at 21:31 (F10), giving the rider no time to arrive within the NS-1(iii) window.
Agreed: ordinary conditions (F13, F14, F15) remove any external excuse, and the ordinary-condition arithmetic (F2, F5, F6) is under 3 minutes, so NS-1(iii) fails and NS-2 requires the $6.61 back.
The driver's clean 90-day record (F17) does not appear in my brief as a basis for any account flag, and I ask for no flag: the outcome requested is solely the refund of the $6.61 under NS-2.

The opponent's own concessions (F6 post-tap wait 1 min 45 s; F2 cumulative 2 min 55 s; pre-tap time cannot be added) confirm every element of NS-2's refund: NS-1(iii) fails, so the $6.61 charged on record (F7) is refunded in full.

Correct as far as it goes: only 1 min 45 s elapsed within 200 m after the 21:29:45 tap (F6), which is below the > 3 min continuous wait NS-1(iii) requires, and pre-tap time is expressly not counted under that clause — so no fee can be defended on this record.

Accepted: the system timeline records arrival at 21:28:35 and cancellation 2 min 55 s later (F5, F4), and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 55 s (F2) — still under the NS-1(iii) threshold.

The tap was valid — 41 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius (F6) — which the rider's own weakness paragraph concedes; because the wait requirement in NS-1(iii) is not met the fee cannot stand, and equally NS-2's account flag does not attach since m_from_pickup_at_tap is 41 m, not > 200 m (F6).
The driver does not rely on the post-trip statement of a 5-minute wait (F12); under the system-record rule it loses to the GPS and timeline values in F2 and F6, so this point is not contested.

The words "waited too long" (F10) describe the driver's own impression, but nothing in the messages or records alleges abuse or bad faith: he announced his presence with a vehicle description at 21:29 (F9), stayed 39 m from the pickup (F3), and his profile shows 1216 trips with 0 upheld no-show disputes (F17) — so the premature cancellation is a judgement lapse on a short wait, not conduct warranting an account flag under NS-2.

Accepted as to the fee: the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F7, F4) is refundable in full because NS-1(iii) fails, which is the outcome my brief already asks for; what is not accepted is any additional rider relief, as no other charge exists (F8) and NS-7 caps the remedy at the fee itself.

This point is not in dispute and is immaterial to a no-show case: with no speed-band records (F13), no incidents (F14) and fair weather (F15) the ordinary driving conditions simply confirm the case turns solely on the waiting arithmetic, not on RD-4.
